Chapter 13: Tab Sync

You will configure Tab Sync once, open a second browser tab, and observe finalized FeatureCell State stay aligned while each tab keeps its own form and presentation state.

This is same-origin browser coordination, not transactional collaboration. The chapter keeps that scope explicit and shows which transient state must remain local to each tab.

Keep the same feature coherent across tabs on one browser origin.

People often open the same application twice: a preference changes in one tab, a draft remains open in another, or an administrative view needs the latest committed record. This chapter keeps those Feature State values aligned across same-origin tabs without pretending that every form interaction is shared collaboration.

Why this boundary matters

Tab Sync shares finalized Feature State while each tab retains its own selection, form, loading, and error experience. The behavior and controller coordinate synchronization at the FeatureCell boundary, so the service and component need no special cross-tab plumbing. This is not a substitute for server-authoritative collaboration, cross-device sync, or a security design for sensitive data.

Use this structure for

  • preferences that should remain consistent in every open tab
  • drafts or cart-like State shared within one browser session
  • administrative views that need the latest committed feature value

By the end of this chapter

You will have the Tab Sync behavior and controller configured as a pair, with finalized character State updating across same-origin tabs while transient page interactions remain local to each tab.

Chapter 13 Starting Point and Synchronization Scope

Start with the completed Chapter 7 project. Tab Sync is a Pro capability; production use requires a valid license. This lab changes configuration, component presentation, and tests. The service does not add cross-tab messaging code.

Shared vs. Local
  • Shared: finalized FeatureCell value identified by the same key on the same origin—scheme, host, and port.
  • Local: selection, unsaved form values, pending confirmation, loading, and error presentation in each tab.
  • Not provided: server authority, authorization, cross-device sync, offline reconciliation, audit history, or collaborative conflict resolution.
Concurrent Edits

This lab demonstrates propagation and transactional consistency. guarantees ordering from sequential edits. Tab Sync transports finalized Feature State and reconciles record-level conflicts by using the Conductor Queue.

Environment Support Checklist
  • Both tabs use the same scheme, host, port, and FeatureCell key.
  • The browser permits the required storage and messaging mechanism.
  • Private or restricted contexts may disable the demonstration.
  • The browser allows the second tab and N tabs to open and all pages remain active and synchronized.
  • Reload both tabs after correcting configuration; do not copy State manually.
Step 1: Configure Tab Sync
↑ top
Simplicity Warning

This lab is incredibly simple. The Tab Sync controller and behavior takes care of all the logic. There are no changes to the example.service.ts, example.component.ts or example.component.html files.

This simplistic functionality is intentional and designed to keep unnecessary logic out of the service and component files.

Tab Sync keeps one State value aligned across browser tabs that share the same origin. You configure the complete feature in app.config.ts: the State behavior shares finalized values, and the controller coordinates the initial State when you open another tab.

Register both on the same . The behavior belongs in the behaviors array and the controller belongs in the controllers array passed to provideFeatureCell(). Nothing changes in the service or component to make synchronization work.

Make the Change
  1. Open the app.config.ts file.
  2. Import withTabSyncStateBehavior and withTabSyncController from .
  3. Add the behavior to the behavior list and the controller to the controller list for the same . 
    {{ appConfigFile().source }}
  4. The Tab Sync controller and behavior are Pro features and require a valid Pro license for production use. To explore them locally without a license, add the devMode and bypassingLicensing attributes to the provideVault configuration. 
    provideVault({
  devMode: true,
  bypassingLicensing: true 
})
What to Look For
  • The behavior and controller are a required pair for this FeatureCell.
  • The configuration owns cross-tab State coordination; the service and component stay focused on their existing responsibilities.
  • Only finalized FeatureCell State is shared with a peer tab.
What the Stale-Form Exercise Proves

The exercise proves only that a peer's committed collection can update while Tab B's unsaved form remains local. It proves that saving the stale form is safe and defines which concurrent write wins.

Step 2: View Tab Sync In Action
↑ top

Once your application reloads, you can open a second tab to observe the Tab Sync behavior in action.

Run and Verify
  1. Tabs
    1. Open Tab A and make sure the application has fully reloaded.
    2. Open Tab B on same application URL.
    3. Duplicate (right-mouse click on the tab) Tab B (now Tab C )
    4. Open Tab D and leave blank.
  2. Add, edit, delete, or reset a character collection in tabs A, B or C.
  3. Return to the other tabs (A, B, or C) and inspect the synchronized character State.
  4. Now in the Tab D navigate to the application URL.
  5. Leave an unsaved edit open in Tab B, commit a change in Tab A, and confirm the committed collection updates while Tab B's transient form remains local. Cancel the stale form before continuing.
What to Look For
  • Committed FeatureCell State values are preserved and updated between tabs, including shared resets.
  • Forms, selection, loading, errors, and other page interactions remain local to the tab where they occur.
  • A failed pipeline attempt does not update a peer tab.
  • The new tab receives State without inheriting transient loading or error metadata from its peer.
Chapter Round-up
↑ top

Your Tab Sync example is complete when the behavior and controller are registered together in app.config.ts, and the View Tab Sync action lets you observe committed character State moving between tabs. The existing service and component continue to own their original responsibilities.

Chapter 13 Summary
  • Cross-tab coordination is structural configuration, not component or service logic.
  • Each tab keeps its local form and presentation state while sharing the finalized FeatureCell value.
  • The same FeatureCell key identifies the State that participates in synchronization.
